mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 530i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 530i engine replacement typically costs £1,500-£4,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £2,200-£5,500 depending on the generation and specialist. Used engines can be found from £600-£2,200.

mainEntity.name: What engine codes were used in the BMW 530i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 530i has used six main engine codes across its production: M30B30 (E12/E28/E34), M60B30 (E34 V8), M54B30 (E39/E60), N52B30 (E60), N53B30 (E60 LCI/F10), and B48B20 (G30). The engine code is stamped on the engine block and can also be verified via your VIN.

mainEntity.name: Is the BMW 530i a reliable car?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the 530i is widely regarded as one of the most reliable 5 Series variants, particularly the M54 and N52 straight-six models. However, age-related issues like cooling system deterioration and oil leaks require proactive maintenance.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW 530i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common issues across all 530i generations are cooling system failure (plastic expansion tank, water pump, thermostat degradation) and oil leaks (valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket). On N53 engines, high-pressure fuel pump and injector issues are also reported.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 530i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your 530i's generation and condition. A pristine E39 530i (£5,000+) or any G30 530i (£15,000-£35,000) easily justifies replacement. A sub-£4,000 E60 or older example requires careful evaluation - assess the car's overall condition, rust, and interior before committing.

mainEntity.name: Can I still find parts for the BMW 530i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all 530i engine families have strong aftermarket and OEM parts support in the UK. The M54, N52, N53 and B48 are particularly well-supported, with specialists stocking timing components, cooling system parts, gaskets, and full rebuilt units.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 530i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 530i has been a mainstay of the 5 Series range since the 1970s, evolving from the original M30 'big six' through V8 and modern turbocharged four-cylinder powerplants. Across seven generations, the 530i badge has consistently represented the sweet spot between performance and refinement in the executive saloon market.

milestones.description: E12 530i launched with M30B30 3.0L inline-six, producing 176-188hp (Bosch L-Jetronic fuel injection)
E34 530i gains M60B30 3.0L V8, 218hp - first V8 in a 5 Series
E60 LCI 530i switches to N53B30 3.0L inline-six, 272hp
F10 530i continues with N53B30 3.0L inline-six, 272hp (Europe only)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 5 Series 530i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 530i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 530i has been powered by six different engine families across its long production run, each with its own character and common issues. While generally reliable, age-related cooling system failures and oil leaks are the most frequent concerns for UK owners. A rebuilt 530i engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cooling System Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series 530i Overheats
problems.affectedModels: BMW 5 Series 530i (all generations, all engine codes)
problems.rootCause: The plastic expansion tanks, water pumps, and thermostats degrade with age and mileage, leading to coolant loss and overheating. This is the single most common failure across all 530i generations.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement expansion tank, water pump, thermostat, hoses, coolant flush
repairOptions.longevity: Ideal preventative maintenance on cars over 60k miles
When catastrophic overheating has caused head gasket or bottom-end failure

problems.recommendation: For most BMW 530i owners, preventative cooling system maintenance is the best value approach. The M54, N52 and N53 engines are fundamentally robust, and catching cooling issues early avoids catastrophic failure. If the engine has overheated badly and suffered head gasket or bottom-end damage, a rebuilt unit with warranty is the safer long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 5 Series 530i engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Leaks - Valve Cover and Oil Filter Housing Gasket Failure
problems.affectedModels: BMW 5 Series 530i (M54, N52, N53, B48 engines)
problems.rootCause: The rubber gaskets harden with heat cycling, leading to oil seepage onto the exhaust manifold (creating a burning smell) or onto the drive belt (risking belt failure and engine seizure).

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of valve cover gasket and/or oil filter housing gasket
repairOptions.longevity: Standard maintenance; recommended when leaks are detected
If oil starvation has caused bearing or timing chain damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - assess whether full replacement cost justifies itself against the 530i's current market value.
problems.recommendation: Gasket replacement is routine maintenance on higher-mileage 530i models. If caught early, this is a straightforward specialist repair. If oil has contaminated the drive belt or caused it to fail, check for further damage before deciding on a full replacement.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 5 Series 530i
finalCta.paragraph: The 530i badge has represented over four decades of BMW engineering excellence, from the M30 'big six' through the V8 era to today's turbocharged B48. With regular preventative maintenance - particularly cooling system attention - your 530i can keep delivering that signature straight-six or refined four-cylinder character for years to come. If replacement is required, EnginesMarket connects you with UK specialists offering rebuilt units with 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery.
